personas.notes: Excellent coverage of high-weight keywords. TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, TDD, unit testing (JUnit/Mockito/Jasmine), Git, AWS, Agile Scrum, SaaS integrations, data synchronization, data transfers, third-party system integrations, and service-oriented frameworks are all explicitly mirrored — strong. Gaps to close: (1) 'Kanban' is entirely absent — add it to the LSEG bullet or Skills alongside Agile Scrum since it is a weight-1.0 ATS keyword. (2) 'SQL-based databases' — you list 'SQL' under Language and 'PostgreSQL' under Database, but the exact JD phrase 'SQL-based databases' is not present; consider mirroring it verbatim in Skills. (3) 'CS Degree' — your degree reads 'MS in Computer Software Engineering'; an ATS keyword-matching on 'Computer Science' may miss it — acceptable but borderline. FORMATTING/PARSEABILITY concerns: the resume uses fontspec with XCharter (requires XeLaTeX/LuaLaTeX) — fine for PDF text layer, but the custom bullet glyph '$\vcenter{\hbox{\small$\bullet$}}$' renders as a math-mode bullet that some ATS parsers may drop or mis-extract; prefer a plain textbullet. The '\&\ ' in the Courses line and heavy negative \vspace values (-18.5pt) risk overlapping text in extraction order. Section headings via \section* are unnumbered and machine-readable — good. Ampersands are properly escaped. Overall the vocabulary alignment is high; only Kanban and the verbatim 'SQL-based databases' phrase materially hurt weighted coverage.

Excellent JD coverage — TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, TDD, SQL, AWS, Agile/Scrum, SRE/post-mortems, and SaaS/third-party integrations all mirrored. Bullets are outcome-driven with strong quantification. However, several claims strain credibility for a mid-level SWE and read as inflated: the LSEG bullet stacking '1.4B daily records,' '200% throughput,' '400K+ users,' AND '90% retrieval / 40% analysis time' in single lines packs too many unrelated metrics — split these and ground each in a specific system. The Dassault tenure (June 2025–Jan 2026) is only ~7 months yet claims a two-tower embedding recommender POC on an '8M+ users' platform plus 99% test coverage plus latency cuts — this compressed scope hurts believability; trim to 2-3 defensible wins. Dual AWS Professional + Associate certs alongside an in-progress MS and only ~2 yrs experience raises an eyebrow. The 'GoonedIn' project name is unprofessional — rename it. Recommend: (1) de-stack multi-metric bullets into single-claim outcomes, (2) add one bullet showing ownership/leadership to signal growth toward the role, (3) verify each percentage is attributable to your specific work, not the team's.

Keyword coverage is excellent — TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, TDD, SQL, AWS, CI/CD, SRE, and service-oriented systems all appear. But several claims will collapse under a 30-minute phone screen. FIX THESE: (1) Dassault bullet 2 claims 'real-time data synchronization latency 25%... over WebSockets, GraphQL, AND React' — React is a UI library, not a data-transfer mechanism; pick a coherent transport story or you'll be caught immediately. (2) LSEG bullet 1 '1.4B daily records' then bullet 2 '400K+ users' then bullet 3 '500+ analysts' — these scale numbers don't cohere; be ready to explain the architecture or trim them. (3) NestJS is described as a 'service-oriented framework such as NestJS' — the phrasing reads like padding to mirror the JD rather than real usage; state concretely what you built in NestJS. (4) 'two-tower embeddings and vector similarity search' on a stakeholder-recommendation POC is a strong ML claim sitting next to no ML background — expect deep questions on training data, negative sampling, serving. (5) '99% test coverage across microservices' is implausibly high and a red flag to any engineer; soften to a defensible figure. (6) The project name 'GoonedIn' is a professional liability — rename it. (7) '200% throughput' + '90% retrieval speed' + '75% incident reduction' stacked in adjacent bullets reads as buzzword/metric inflation; keep the two you can whiteboard. Tenure (June 2025–Jan 2026 at Dassault while MS expected Dec 2026) is only 7 months and overlaps school — fine for an internship but label it if so. Formatting is clean and ATS-safe.

Most reframings are defensible. Two items warrant interview-prep caution. LSEG bullet 2 claims Node.js microservices 'compatible with service-oriented frameworks such as NestJS' — source_evidence only says Spring Boot + asynchronous processing; NestJS does not appear anywhere in the source and is being inserted to mirror the JD. This is the single most important must_mirror keyword, and a phone screen asking 'tell me about your NestJS work' could expose it. Recommend either grounding this in actual NestJS experience or softening the claim. TDD framing in Dassault bullet 1 ('applying Test-Driven Development principles') is an addition to source evidence which only lists test coverage tooling — plausible for an engineer maintaining 99% coverage, but be ready to discuss TDD workflow specifically. Dassault bullet 3 adds 'wiring in third-party system integrations for data exchange' to the recommendation POC — the source POC description makes no mention of integrations; this is adjacent-plausible but thinly supported, keep scope honest. React changed from JavaScript (source) to TypeScript in the latency bullet — minor and defensible given TS is a listed skill. Scale/metrics (1.4B records, 200% throughput, 90% retrieval) all trace cleanly to source. Overall the backend/financial-systems/SaaS framings hold; primary risk is the NestJS insertion.
